I farm here in the North West, and this sorghum plot of 1.36 hectares is my main food for the family. I will put some NPK and urea if I can get them from the agro-dealer, because the soil is tired and sorghum needs help to yield well, but I cannot afford full dose. I keep my own sorghum seed from last year like my father did — improved seed is expensive and not always available here. I intercrop with cowpea as usual, and I will add the little manure I have from my goats and sheep around the compound.
